area: settings (general / appearance / location / files-storage / connection / settings shell)
verified_correct: settings:general - all three switches (Start minimized, Auto-connect equipment, Confirm before closing) write through to app_settings immediately and the rendered switch matches the DB after a page revisit; attacked by flipping each and re-reading sqlite3.

settings:location - latitude/longitude/elevation commit when you navigate away WITHOUT blurring the field first (typed 1234 into Elevation then clicked Dashboard in the nav rail; observer_elevation was 1234.0). This is the classic uncommitted-edit data-loss case and it is handled.
settings:location - out-of-range latitude is clamped and the field is rewritten to match: typed 95, DB stored 90.0 AND the field re-rendered as 90, so UI and DB agree.

settings:location - twilight math is right. With 47.6062/-122.3321 the dashboard gave Sunset 23:48, Astro dark 02:00, Astro dawn 06:31, Sunrise 08:43 in host-local EDT; an independent NOAA-algorithm calculation gives 23:44 / 02:02 / 06:28 / 08:47 (all within the 2-4 min accuracy of that approximation).

settings:location - horizon import rejects malformed input precisely and non-destructively: a file containing 'hello world' produced 'Could not import horizon: Horizon import line 1: non-numeric value in "hello world"' and left the previously imported profile intact in the DB.
settings:location - Bortle class -> limiting magnitude follows the published Bortle table (1 -> 7.6m, 5 -> 5.9m, 9 -> 4.0m) and the subtitle updates to name the class it is quoting.

settings:appearance - Light theme is fully applied, not half-done: sampled the title bar, nav rail, settings sidebar, page background, card and status bar; all are light (255,255,255 / 244,246,248). Accent colour selection propagates to the nav selection and the swatch ring.
settings:appearance - Font size Large visibly enlarges every label app-wide, and the collapsed nav rail shows a correct name+subtitle tooltip on hover (verified 'Sequencer / Automation').
settings:appearance - the settings sidebar scrolls at UI scale 1.4x, so ADVANCED stays reachable.

findings.title: Selecting Spanish translates only the nav rail and Settings; every other screen stays English
findings.what_happened: Settings > General > Language > Spanish. The nav rail and the whole Settings tree translate correctly (Ajustes/Apariencia/Ubicacion/Archivos y almacenamiento) and app_settings.language flips to 'es'. But the Dashboard renders 100% English: 'TONIGHT'S BRIEFING', 'No run active', 'Image tonight', 'Plan Tonight', 'Set an observing location for twilight times.', "Tonight's targets", 'Readiness', 'Edit Dashboard'. The persistent bottom status bar is also English on every screen ('Camera Disconnected', 'Mount Disconnected', 'Guider Disconnected', 'Focus', 'No save path', 'Dashboard'). The Spanish subtitle under the setting reads 'Elegir el idioma de la interfaz principal' (choose the language of the MAIN interface), which is not what it does.
findings.expected: Either translate the product surfaces too, or label the control honestly and scope it (the English subtitle 'app chrome' is closer to the truth than the Spanish one). Shipping a language picker that leaves the main working screens untranslated is worse than not offering the language.
findings.repro: Fresh profile -> Settings > General -> Language dropdown -> Spanish -> click Dashboard in nav rail -> tree shows all English strings.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/05-spanish.png (Settings fully Spanish, status bar English); tree of Dashboard after switching: 0 of ~12 visible dashboard strings translated. sqlite3 app_settings language='es'.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/general_settings.dart:79-93 (SettingsDropdown offers languageEnglish/languageSpanish); localization coverage in packages/skotiq_app/lib/localization/
findings.proposed_fix: Either finish the es catalogue for the dashboard/imaging/sequencer surfaces, or hide the Spanish option behind a flag until it is complete.

findings.title: Red night mode leaves the Moon phase disc near-white — a dark-adaptation flare on the default screen
findings.what_happened: With Theme = Red night, the Dashboard's Moon card renders a ~50 px filled disc at RGB(214,220,226) (luminance 219) on a background of RGB(10,0,0). It is by far the brightest object on screen and it is bluish-white, exactly the wavelength red-night mode exists to suppress. Everything else on the dashboard is correctly red-shifted.
findings.expected: Red night should red-shift or dim the moon graphic like everything else (e.g. desaturate to a red-grey ramp). A user at the eyepiece opens the dashboard and gets a white disc in the face.
findings.repro: Settings > Appearance > Theme > Red night, then click Dashboard in the nav rail. Moon card, left column.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/10-rednight-dash.png; sampled pixel (293,416) = (214,220,226) vs page background (600,600) = (10,0,0). Brightest pixel in the whole frame is inside the disc at (302,390) = (229,238,244).
findings.where: Dashboard moon-phase widget (moon card) — theme-independent colours; theme applied in skotiq_ui red night theme.
findings.proposed_fix: Drive the moon disc fill/limb colours from the theme's surface/onSurface ramp instead of hardcoded greys, so Red night maps them to dim red.

findings.title: Red night mode still paints the accent-colour swatches in full-saturation cyan, green and magenta
findings.what_happened: Settings > Appearance under Theme = Red night shows the 7 accent swatches at their literal colours: sampled (16,185,129) green, (245,158,11) amber, (6,182,212) cyan, (236,72,153) magenta. On the same page every other pixel is red-shifted.
findings.expected: Either suppress the swatch row in red night (the accent has no visible effect in a monochrome red theme anyway), or dim/annotate it. As shipped, opening Appearance at the telescope to check the theme is the thing that ruins your dark adaptation.
findings.repro: Settings > Appearance > Theme > Red night; the Accent color row is directly under Theme.
findings.proposed_fix: Hide or grey the accent row when theme == redNight, or render each swatch as a red-luminance equivalent with a small label.

findings.title: At UI scale Extra Large (1.4x) the bottom status bar overlaps itself — the run-state chip is painted under the temperature group
findings.what_happened: Settings > Appearance > UI scale = Extra Large (1.4x) (Font size Large). The persistent bottom status bar stops laying out and two groups collide: the 'Idle' run-state chip is clipped to 'Idl' and the thermometer/'- - -' group is drawn on top of it. The status bar is present on every screen, so this is app-wide, not a Settings-only glitch.
findings.expected: The status bar should drop or scroll items when it runs out of width, never overlap them. NINA collapses status items into an overflow chevron.
findings.repro: Settings > Appearance: Font size = Large, UI scale = Extra Large (1.4x). Look at the bottom bar between the Focus chip and 'No save path'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/13-xlscale.png and the 4x crop /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/13-statusbar-crop.png, which shows 'Idl' with the thermometer glyph painted over the final letter.
findings.where: app shell bottom status bar (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/) — driven by ui_scale from appearance settings
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the status groups in a Flexible/Wrap with ellipsis per group, or hide the lowest-priority groups below a width threshold.

findings.title: UI scale dropdown truncates its own selected value to 'Extra Lar...' at large UI scale
findings.what_happened: With UI scale = Extra Large (1.4x) the dropdown that sets it renders 'Extra Lar...' — the control cannot display the value it currently holds because SettingsDropdown is given a fixed 150 px width that does not scale.
findings.expected: The dropdown width should scale with ui_scale/font size, or the labels should be short enough ('1.4x') to survive.
findings.repro: Settings > Appearance > UI scale > Extra Large (1.4x).
findings.proposed_fix: Make the dropdown width intrinsic (IntrinsicWidth / min-width) instead of a hardcoded 150.

findings.title: Timezone picker is inert: all 18 options are IANA names, and the clock parser accepts none of them — every displayed time silently stays on the host's timezone
findings.what_happened: Settings > Location > Time: I turned 'Use system time' OFF and set Timezone = America/Los_Angeles, then Asia/Tokyo, then UTC. app_settings.timezone and use_system_time persist correctly each time, but NOTHING on screen changes: the status-bar clock stayed 14:44 (host America/New_York) when it should have read 11:44 PDT / 03:44 JST / 18:44 UTC, the Dashboard header clock stayed host-local, and the Dashboard twilight strip stayed byte-identical (Sunset 23:48 / Astro dark 02:00 / Astro dawn 06:31 / Sunrise 08:43) across all three timezones. Root cause in source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/clock_provider.dart:219 _parseTimezoneOffset accepts only 'UTC' or 'UTC+HH[:MM]' and returns null for anything else, so clockProvider falls back to SystemClock for all 17 IANA entries the picker offers. The fallback is completely silent — the file's own comment claims 'Failure to parse is explicit and logged at the Clock.fromUtc call sites', but nothing appears in app.log (grep for timezone/clock/tz over the whole 151-line log: zero hits).
findings.expected: Picking a site timezone must change displayed times, or the picker must not exist. clockProvider feeds imaging_service capture timestamps, session_provider and scheduler_provider, so a remote-observatory operator who sets the site timezone gets host-local timestamps on their frames and host-local scheduler decisions while the UI shows the timezone they chose.
findings.repro: Settings > Location, scroll to Time. Toggle 'Use system time' OFF. Set Timezone = Asia/Tokyo. Look at the status-bar clock and at Dashboard > twilight strip. Repeat with America/Los_Angeles and UTC.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/24-status.png (LA, sys-time on: 14:43), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/25-status.png (LA, sys-time OFF: 14:44 — unchanged), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/27-status.png (Asia/Tokyo, sys-time OFF: 14:44), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/31-status.png (UTC, sys-time OFF: 14:46 while `date -u` says 18:46), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/28-crop.png (twilight strip unchanged under Asia/Tokyo). sqlite3 confirms timezone/use_system_time persisted each time.
findings.proposed_fix: Either store real IANA zones and resolve them with the `timezone` package (correct, handles DST), or change the picker to emit the UTC+HH:MM labels the parser already understands. At minimum make the fallback loud instead of silent.

findings.title: Timezone list is 18 hardcoded cities — most of the world cannot select their site's timezone
findings.what_happened: The Timezone dropdown offers exactly: UTC, America/{New_York,Chicago,Denver,Los_Angeles,Phoenix,Anchorage}, Pacific/Honolulu, Europe/{London,Paris,Berlin,Moscow}, Asia/{Tokyo,Shanghai,Kolkata}, Australia/{Sydney,Perth}, Pacific/Auckland. There is no free-text entry and no search. All of South America, Africa, the Middle East, Scandinavia, Spain/Portugal, Canada, Mexico and most of Asia are unrepresented — including Chile and Namibia, where a large fraction of remote-hosted amateur rigs actually sit.
findings.expected: A searchable IANA zone list (as NINA and every OS settings panel provide), or — better for an astro app — derive the site timezone from the lat/long that is already entered three rows above, with an override.
findings.evidence: tree of the open popup lists all 18 entries; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/23-crop.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/29-crop.png.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with a searchable IANA list, plus a 'from location' button that resolves lat/long -> tz.

findings.title: Location has no place search — you must know your decimal latitude and longitude
findings.what_happened: Settings > Location offers three bare numeric fields (Latitude, Longitude, Elevation) plus 'Sync from Server' and 'Use Device Location'. There is no city/place lookup, no DMS entry, and no map picker. A new user who knows they observe from 'Bend, Oregon' has to leave the app to find 44.0582 / -121.3153 / 1100 m.
findings.expected: ASIAIR and SkySafari let you pick a city; NINA accepts DMS and can pull from the mount. At minimum accept DMS input ('47 36 22 N') in the same field, and offer an offline city list — the app already ships large catalogs.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a DMS-tolerant parser to the lat/long fields and a bundled city picker; optionally 'read from connected mount'.

findings.title: 'Use Device Location' is IP geolocation labelled as GPS, and it leaves the old elevation in place — producing a site that does not exist
findings.what_happened: The row reads 'Use Device Location / Get location from GPS'. Clicking it on Linux desktop returned 'Location updated: Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, United States' and wrote observer_latitude=39.9817, observer_longitude=-75.4072 — but observer_elevation stayed at 1234.0, the value from the previous (Seattle) site. The stored site is now a Pennsylvania coordinate at 1234 m; the highest point in Pennsylvania is 979 m. The success message says 'Location updated' with no hint that one of the three fields was not updated. Source: location_settings.dart:270 passes `elevation: settings.elevation` unchanged, and GeolocationService.fetchLocationFromGPS() (packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/services/geolocation_service.dart:7-14) is not GPS at all — it does an HTTPS GET to the third-party service https://ipapi.co/json/.
findings.expected: (a) Do not call it GPS when it is IP geolocation — say 'Estimate from IP address (city-level, ~10 km)'. (b) Either fetch/clear elevation, or say plainly that elevation was not changed and needs review. (c) Disclose that clicking sends the user's IP to a third party before doing it — this is a silent outbound request from an app people run on isolated observatory networks.
findings.repro: Settings > Location > set elevation to 1234 and latitude 47.6062 (Seattle). Click the crosshair on 'Use Device Location'. Read the snackbar, then sqlite3 app_settings observer_*.
findings.evidence: Snackbar text captured via tree: 'Location updated: Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, United States'. sqlite3 immediately after: observer_latitude|39.9817, observer_longitude|-75.4072, observer_elevation|1234.0.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename the row, blank or refetch elevation alongside lat/long, and gate the network call behind an explicit one-time consent.

findings.title: 'Sync from Server' reports 'Location synced from server' on a standalone desktop session where there is no server
findings.what_happened: With the app running standalone (no headless host paired, backend = local), clicking the download-cloud on 'Sync from Server / Fetch location from Headless Server' shows a green success snackbar 'Location synced from server'. Nothing was fetched from any server: the handler calls profileSettingsBackendProvider.getLocation(), which on a local session returns the location this same app just wrote, so the values were unchanged (47.6062 / -122.3321 / 1234 before and after).
findings.expected: The row should be hidden or disabled when no headless host is connected — exactly the way the same file already hides 'Start minimized' and 'Confirm before closing' in remote mode. A green 'synced from server' when there is no server is a false claim, and it trains the user to trust that message when it matters.
findings.repro: Fresh desktop profile, no pairing. Settings > Location > click the icon on the 'Sync from Server' row.
findings.evidence: tree captured the snackbar 'Location synced from server'; sqlite3 app_settings observer_* identical before and after the click.
findings.proposed_fix: Gate the row on isRemoteMode / a connected host, and word the success as 'Location read from <host>'.

findings.title: Importing a detailed .hor horizon silently collapses it to 8 sector maxima — a single tree blocks a whole 45-degree sector
findings.what_happened: I imported a 36-point .hor file (one sample every 10 deg of azimuth, altitudes 10-29 deg). The snackbar said 'Horizon profile imported from test36.hor' and the eight compass fields filled in as N=25, NE=16, E=21, SE=25, S=29, SW=14, W=19, NW=23. Those are exactly the MAXIMUM sample in each 45 deg sector — the other 28 samples were discarded with no mention. Source confirms this is deliberate (location_settings.dart:498-501, 'highest altitude per sector wins'), but nothing in the UI says so.
findings.expected: Real horizon files from Stellarium/HorizonBox have 1-degree resolution and are the reason people generate them. Max-per-sector means one 29-degree tree at azimuth 190 marks everything from 157.5 to 202.5 as blocked, so the planner and Tonight will refuse targets that are actually clear — this costs imaging time on exactly the targets a southern-horizon site cares about. At minimum the import must say 'imported 36 samples, reduced to 8 sectors (worst case per sector)'. Better: store the full profile and interpolate.
findings.repro: Create a .hor with one line per 10 deg azimuth; Settings > Location > Local Horizon Mask > Import .hor / CSV; compare the eight resulting fields with the file.
findings.evidence: Input /tmp/ns-audit/rsg-files/test36.hor; resulting horizon_profile_json from sqlite3: {"N":25.0,"NE":16.0,"E":21.0,"SE":25.0,"S":29.0,"SW":14.0,"W":19.0,"NW":23.0} — verified by hand to be the per-sector maxima. Snackbar text captured from tree.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist the full sampled profile and interpolate at query time; keep the 8 fields as a coarse editor/summary. Failing that, report the sample count and the reduction in the success message.

findings.title: 'Reset All to 0 deg' wipes an imported horizon with no confirmation, one click from the Import button
findings.what_happened: 'Import .hor / CSV' and 'Reset All to 0 deg' sit side by side on the same row, ~120 px apart. Clicking Reset immediately set horizon_profile_json to all zeros. No confirm dialog, no undo, and the imported file is not remembered, so recovering means finding the .hor again.
findings.expected: Confirm before discarding a non-zero horizon, or offer undo in the snackbar.
findings.repro: Import a horizon, then click 'Reset All to 0 deg' on the same row.
findings.evidence: horizon_profile_json went from {"N":25.0,...} to {"N":0.0,"NE":0.0,...} with no prompt; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/33-afterimport.png shows the two buttons adjacent.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a confirm when any value is non-zero, or an 'Undo' action on the snackbar.
